questions.question: What is the minimum color contrast ratio required by WCAG 2.1 AA for normal body text against its background?
questions.explanation: WCAG 2.1 AA mandates a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text (under 18pt).

questions.question: Which media query detects if a user has requested their operating system to minimize non-essential animations?
questions.explanation: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) allows developers to respect user vestibular accessibility settings.

questions.question: Why is relying solely on color (such as red vs green text) to indicate form errors an accessibility failure?
options: Colorblind users cannot distinguish red from green, leaving errors invisible without text labels or icons
Red text fails to render on mobile
questions.explanation: WCAG requires that information conveyed by color must also be communicated via text, icons, or underline patterns.

questions.question: What is the minimum WCAG contrast ratio required for active UI components, buttons, and form borders?
questions.hint: 3:1 for graphical elements and large text.
questions.explanation: WCAG 2.1 requires a minimum 3:1 contrast ratio for user interface components and graphical boundaries.

questions.question: Which media query adapts styling for Windows High Contrast Mode?
questions.explanation: @media (forced-colors: active) targets operating system high-contrast environments.
